The main takeaway from our work is that

the thermodynamic stability of a metal oxide electrode surface is strongly influenced by the stoichiometry of the surface, with the highest reduction drive for surfaces that are deficient in the metal oxide cation.
the thermodynamic stability of a surface can be strongly affected by the surface stoichiometry and that this can have a strong impact on the reduction drive of the surface.
